title_en: Gebu Schemarker Limited Partnership v. Shanghai Foreign Trade Corporation — dispute over transfer of ship-attached debt
keywords_en: civil; dispute over debt transfer; first instance; intermediate people's court; Shanghai; legal person; foreign-invested enterprise; Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Trial Implementation); maritime lien; debt transfer; limitation of action; partial support; supply of ship chandlery; bank guarantee; guarantee; dispute over debt transfer accompanying the vessel of Yi General Company
full_text_en:
Gebr. Schumacher Limited Partnership

v. Shanghai Foreign Trade Corporation

— Dispute over ship-attached debt transfer

Plaintiff: Gebr. Schumacher Limited Partnership.

Defendant: Shanghai Foreign Trade Corporation.

The plaintiff, Gebr. Schumacher Limited Partnership of the Federal Republic of Germany, filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court against the defendant, Shanghai Foreign Trade Corporation, on the ground that the vessel M/V Bellpe, purchased by the defendant, carried a ship-attached debt of over DM 35,000, and claimed payment of the debt.

After accepting the case, the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court ascertained the following facts: On August 15, 1983, the M/V Bellpe, owned by Panama Ocean King Navigation Company, was at the port of Constanța, Romania, and requested the plaintiff to supply a batch of deck stores, mechanical spare parts, and foodstuffs. The plaintiff, in accordance with the request, shipped the goods in three lots from Bremen to the M/V Bellpe in August and September of the same year, and issued five invoices totaling DM 35,561.72. The cargo list was signed and sealed by the ship's master. After the expiry of the agreed 30-day payment term, the plaintiff repeatedly pressed the shipowner for payment but received no results.

On December 22, 1983, Panama Ocean King Navigation Company entered into a contract with the defendant to sell the M/V Bellpe for USD 437,402, with the delivery date set for no later than January 15, 1984. Upon learning of this, the plaintiff notified the defendant by telex on January 6, 1984, stating that the M/V Bellpe still had outstanding debts and claimed a priority right of satisfaction against the vessel. On January 10, the defendant telegraphed Panama Ocean King Navigation Company, stating that it could only take delivery of the vessel if the plaintiff's lawyer certified that the vessel owed no debt to the plaintiff. On January 11, Panama Ocean King Navigation Company replied, stating that although the plaintiff's claim was unreasonable, it was willing to provide a bank guarantee of DM 44,000 as compensation for losses if the defendant became involved in litigation in order to facilitate the vessel transaction. On January 13, Panama Ocean King Navigation Company, through the Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken of Switzerland, commissioned the Bank of China, Shanghai Branch, to provide the defendant with a guarantee of DM 44,000 (of which DM 34,000 was for the cargo claim and DM 10,000 for litigation costs). The guarantee agreement entered into between the Bank of China, Shanghai Branch, and Panama Ocean King Navigation Company stipulated that the plaintiff's claim must be filed no later than December 31, 1984. Subsequently, on January 16, 1984, the defendant completed the handover procedures for the M/V Bellpe.

Having repeatedly urged the defendant for payment without result, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court on June 7, 1984, asserting that "the nature of this claim is a priority claim attached to the vessel." On July 4, the defendant answered, arguing that there was no creditor-debtor relationship between the defendant and the plaintiff, that the defendant did not become the plaintiff's debtor simply because of the transfer of ownership of the vessel, and moreover, the vessel had already been dismantled before the plaintiff filed the lawsuit; that according to relevant international practice, the plaintiff's claim had exceeded the six-month statute of limitations; and that the bank guarantee was provided by Panama Ocean King Navigation Company in accordance with the defendant's conditions for taking delivery of the vessel, and was not issued in response to the plaintiff's claim.

During the trial of this case, the authorized agents of the plaintiff and the defendant held out-of-court negotiations, and both parties agreed that the defendant would pay 50% of the cargo price to settle the dispute. The plaintiff telegraphed its authorized agent, stating: "Although we do not fully agree with your explanation, we accept this settlement." Accordingly, the parties reached an agreement. The Shanghai Intermediate People's Court reviewed the agreement and found that it did not clearly define the defendant's liability, that the plaintiff's consent was not entirely voluntary, and that the content of the agreement was manifestly unfair; therefore, the court did not approve the agreement.

On September 28, 1984, the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court conducted a public hearing of the case. In accordance with Chinese law and relevant international practice, the court confirmed the following: The creditor-debtor relationship between the plaintiff and Panama Ocean King Navigation Company arising from the plaintiff's supply of goods to the M/V Bellpe was evidenced by the invoices issued by the plaintiff and the receipt signed by the M/V Bellpe, while the defendant failed to produce evidence that the shipowner had already discharged the debt; before taking delivery of the M/V Bellpe, the defendant was aware that the vessel owed debts to the plaintiff, but after Panama Ocean King Navigation Company provided a corresponding bank guarantee for the plaintiff's claim, the defendant paid the full purchase price and completed the handover procedures, which indicated that the defendant had accepted the transfer of the debt of the M/V Bellpe; the defendant's argument that there was no creditor-debtor relationship with the plaintiff and that it did not become the plaintiff's debtor due to the transfer of ownership of the vessel was untenable; the dismantling of the vessel occurred after the plaintiff had asserted its claim against the defendant and after Panama Ocean King Navigation Company had provided the guarantee, so this did not result in the extinction of the debt; with respect to the statute of limitations issue, the plaintiff had, within six months after the expiry of the agreed payment period, separately asserted its rights against Panama Ocean King Navigation Company and the defendant, and in the guarantee agreement issued by Panama Ocean King Navigation Company through the Bank of China, Shanghai Branch, a deadline of December 31, 1984 was set for accepting claims against this possible debt dispute, which should be regarded as an interruption of the statute of limitations, and the plaintiff's lawsuit was filed within the claims period. Accordingly, this debt and claim should be recognized. Under the circumstance that the defendant knew that the M/V Bellpe had a debt dispute, it agreed to accept the bank guarantee provided by Panama Ocean King Navigation Company and then proceeded to take delivery of the vessel and pay the purchase price; this should be regarded as the defendant's acceptance of the transferred debt of the M/V Bellpe. Therefore, the defendant was obliged to repay the said debt to the plaintiff.

After the court conducted the public hearing in accordance with the law, the defendant, pursuant to Article 45, paragraph 1, of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), requested mediation. The plaintiff agreed.

On October 27, 1984, in accordance with Article 97 of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), and on the basis of having ascertained the facts and distinguished right from wrong, and also in consideration of the fact that the plaintiff had taken into account the limit of the guarantee amount of DM 34,000 for the cargo claim accepted by the defendant, the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court reached the following mediation agreement:

1. The defendant shall, no later than November 10, 1984, repay to the plaintiff the guarantee of DM 34,000 provided by Panama Ocean King Navigation Company to the defendant for the purpose of paying the plaintiff's cargo claim.

2. The litigation costs of DM 711.23 shall be paid by the defendant from the guarantee for litigation costs provided by Panama Ocean King Navigation Company and accepted by the defendant.

3. The attorneys' fees of the plaintiff and the defendant shall be borne by each party respectively.

At its 232nd meeting on August 17, 1985, the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, in accordance with Article 11, paragraph 1, of the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China, and in summarizing trial experience, considered that in its handling of this case, the Shanghai Intermediate People's Court had distinguished right from wrong, clarified liability, and lawfully protected the legitimate rights and interests of the foreign party.
